title: Volkswagen Nivus gets new hybrid generation and expanded discounts for PcD
seoTitle: Volkswagen Nivus Hybrid & Expanded PcD Discounts
subtitle: Testing of hybrid version in Europe and increased rebates for people with disabilities boost the model in Brazil
excerpt: Volkswagen signals the arrival of a full hybrid Nivus in its second generation and expands discounts for PcD, generating great interest among consumers.
author: Daniele Morais
sourceName: Motor1.com Brasil, Mundo do Automóvel para PCD
contentHtml:
Recent revelations regarding the new generation of the Volkswagen Nivus and higher discounts for buyers with disabilities have put the model in the automotive news spotlight. What was once just a compact SUV is now drawing attention on two fronts: advanced electrification being tested in Europe and more advantageous pricing conditions for the PcD audience in Brazil.

Mild hybrid Nivus testing in Europe

According to a report by Motor1.com Brasil, the European model equivalent to the Nivus, the Volkswagen Taigo, was spotted testing without camouflage featuring a 48-volt mild hybrid system (MHEV). The setup uses the four-cylinder 1.5 eTSI engine, an evolved version of the 1.4 TSI 250, delivering 116 or 150 hp. The presence of this system meets European Union emission reduction requirements and creates competition against Asian rivals already advancing in the European market.

New generation of the Nivus in Brazil with full hybrid

Nationwide, the second generation of the Nivus will follow a different path. The MQB37 platform, successor to the MQB A0, allows for the adoption of a full hybrid system (HEV) derived from the T-Roc and Golf models. The engine delivers 170 hp and 31.6 kgfm of torque, capable of operating in 100% electric mode up to 55 km/h when demand does not exceed 20 hp. The 1.6 kWh battery is liquid-cooled beneath the rear seat.

Expanded discounts for PcD buyers

In September 2026, Volkswagen increased the rebate granted to people with disabilities. The Nivus Comfortline 200 TSI, which costs R$ 158,290 on the public price list, is now sold for R$ 126,342.58, representing a discount of R$ 31,947.42. The Highline 200 TSI has a public price of R$ 173,290 and drops to R$ 141,569.63 for PcD, with a reduction of R$ 31,720.37. Meanwhile, the GTS 250 TSI, listed at R$ 193,290, is priced at R$ 165,168.84, yielding a rebate of R$ 28,121.16. The Comfortline model features the largest price drop among the three versions.

Powertrains of the PcD versions

The Comfortline and Highline versions use the 1.0 200 TSI turboflex engine, which develops up to 128 hp and 20.4 kgfm of torque. The top-of-the-line Nivus GTS receives the 1.4 250 TSI turboflex engine, with 150 hp and 25.5 kgfm of torque. All versions are equipped with a six-speed automatic transmission.

Impact on the Brazilian market

The combination of a larger Nivus—with a projected length of around 4.50 m, approaching the mid-size segment—and the offering of full hybrid technology indicates Volkswagen's intention to compete directly with models like the Toyota Corolla Cross and Jeep Compass. At the same time, the expanded discounts for PcD make the model more accessible to this audience, broadening the potential buyer base.

With information from Motor1.com Brasil, Mundo do Automóvel para PCD.
